pll2d10c1-d1e3514.summary: Asks whether all heavenly spirits are sent to announce outward things.

pll2d10c1-d1e3517.summary: Reports some who think some spirits go out for their office while others always stand within, citing Dan 7:10: thousands ministered to him and ten thousand stood before him.
claims: Some angels minister outwardly, others stand within.

pll2d10c1-d1e3534.summary: Cites Dionysius's Hierarchy: the higher ranks never leave the inner court, since those who are preeminent never have the use of an outer office.
claims: The higher orders are never sent.

pll2d10c1-d1e3553.summary: Notes that those who deny that any but lower angels are sent rely on these authorities.

pll2d10c1-d1e3556.summary: Objects with Isa 6:6, 'one of the Seraphim flew to me,' the highest order, so others are sent too; and Heb 1:14, 'all are ministering spirits sent to serve.'

pll2d10c1-d1e3586.summary: Reports that by these texts some assert all angels are sent, which is not unworthy, since the Creator of all descended to these lower things.
claims: The Creator's descent shows sending is not unworthy.

pll2d10c1-d1e3589.summary: Asks why, if all are sent as God's messengers, only one of the nine orders is called Angels.

pll2d10c1-d1e3592.summary: Reports the answer: all are sent, but some more often as by assigned office, properly called Angels and Archangels, others, the greater ones, rarely, for a cause outside the common dispensation, taking the name when they take up the ministry.
claims: Some are sent by office, others for special causes.

pll2d10c1-d1e3595.summary: Cites Ps 103:4, 'he makes his angels spirits': those who are spirits by nature sometimes become angels, that is messengers.
claims: 'Angel' names an office, not a nature.

pl-l2d10c1.summary: Asks whether all heavenly spirits are sent to announce outwardly. Some think some go out on mission while others always stand within (Dan 7:10), and Dionysius says the higher ranks never leave the inner court. But Isaiah says one of the Seraphim flew to him (Isa 6:6), and Paul says all are ministering spirits sent to serve (Heb 1:14), so some hold all are sent, which is not unworthy, since the Creator himself descended. Why then is only one order named 'Angels' (messengers)? Some say all are sent, but some often as by assigned office (Angels and Archangels), others rarely for special causes, taking the name when they take the ministry; 'he makes his angels spirits' (Ps 103:4) means those who are spirits by nature sometimes become messengers.
claims: Some hold only the lower angels are sent, the higher always assisting.
Others hold all angels are sent, citing Isaiah 6:6 and Hebrews 1:14.
It is not unworthy for higher angels to be sent, since the Creator descended.
Some are sent often by office, others rarely for special causes.
Angels are spirits by nature and messengers by office.
